title: US Sanctions Three Turkish Firms in Iran Crackdown as Erdoğan Hosts Envoy Barrack
subhead: Washington added three Turkey-based companies to its Iran sanctions list under 'Operation Economic Outcast,' while Erdoğan met US Ambassador and Syria-Iraq envoy Tom Barrack in Ankara — a day of simultaneous financial pressure and diplomatic outreach on the US-Turkey front.

sections.heading: Foreign Relations: US Sanctions Three Turkish Firms Over Mahan Air Ties
sections.body:
The US Treasury's OFAC added Sky Phoenix Airways, S Sistem Logistics and MES Cargo to its sanctions list on Tuesday, Turkish Minute reports, accusing them of helping Iran's Mahan Air obtain US-origin aircraft and move drone components. Sky Phoenix, registered in İzmir, and UAE-based ECT Aviation Support allegedly served as intermediaries in the transfer of at least three Boeing 777 aircraft to Mahan Air this summer, while S Sistem coordinated shipments of UAV components and MES Kargo acted as the Iranian carrier's general sales agent.

The designations were part of a broader action targeting 36 entities, including 27 Iranian airlines and aviation firms. Turkish Minute notes the move came four days after Washington sanctioned İstanbul-based Golden Global Bank, putting six Turkey-based entities on US lists in five days under 'Operation Economic Outcast,' Washington's campaign to cut Iran off from international financial and transport networks. The Turkish government had not issued a public response as of Wednesday.
sections.whyItMatters: The sanctions extend US financial pressure directly into Turkey's transport and logistics sector, testing whether Ankara will push back or quietly accommodate Washington's Iran campaign even as it deepens economic ties with Moscow.

sections.heading: Foreign Relations: Erdoğan Receives US Envoy Barrack and Rep. Issa
sections.body:
President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan received US Ambassador to Türkiye and special envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack and US Rep. Darrell Issa in Ankara, Daily Sabah reports, as diplomatic contacts between the two governments intensify. The meeting came the same day Washington announced fresh sanctions on Turkish firms, underscoring the mix of pressure and engagement that now defines the bilateral relationship.

Barrack's dual role as ambassador and Syria-Iraq envoy gives the meeting direct relevance to Ankara's core regional concerns — the PKK disarmament process in Iraq and the situation in Syria, where Türkiye extended condolences Wednesday for an Idlib weapons depot blast that killed at least 14 people, according to Anadolu Agency.
sections.whyItMatters: The timing — sanctions and a high-level meeting on the same day — shows Washington is running a dual-track policy toward Ankara: financial pressure on Iran-related activity alongside direct engagement on Syria and Iraq, where Turkish cooperation matters.

sections.heading: Kurdish Peace Process: Turkey, Iraq and KRG Plan for 4,200 PKK Members to Disarm
sections.body:
Officials from Turkey, Iraq and the Kurdistan Regional Government are meeting in Erbil over a plan for some 4,200 PKK members to lay down their arms and vacate 18 sites this month, Turkish Minute reports, citing the Iraqi outlet Al Aalem Al Jadid. A group comprising Turkey's MİT, the Iraqi National Security Service and the Kurdistan Region Security Council has been holding daily talks in the city.

The first stage covers positions in Amedi, Kani Masi, Zakho, Avashin, Said Sadiq, Ranya, Dukan, Koya, Mount Korek and Sidakan — but not Mount Qandil, where the PKK's main command is based. Security teams are monitoring 72 PKK positions near the Turkish border, and MİT teams are expected to inspect vacated sites for weapons and explosives. Handover points have been selected in Duhok, Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, though the parties have yet to agree on who receives the weapons; senior PUK official Ghiyath Surji said Baghdad should, since the handovers occur on Iraqi soil. Iraqi Armed Forces spokesman Sabah Noman confirmed a joint mechanism but did not confirm the 4,200 figure, and a separate account put the number at about 3,800.
sections.whyItMatters: A concrete, staged disarmament plan is taking shape on the ground — with Qandil deliberately deferred — but the unresolved question of who collects the weapons shows how fragile the mechanics remain between Ankara, Baghdad and Erbil.

sections.heading: Defense: Turkish Pilots Begin Eurofighter Flight Training in UK
sections.body:
Turkish Air Force pilots have begun flight training on Eurofighter Typhoon jets in the United Kingdom after completing an introductory aviation terminology course, Turkey's Defense Ministry announced Wednesday, Turkish Minute reports. The training is part of the agreement under which Turkey will purchase 20 newly built Typhoons from the UK.

The ministry said the flight training will last eight months, followed by a three-month instructor pilot course. The £8 billion deal, signed in October 2025, has first delivery expected in 2030, with BAE Systems carrying out final assembly at its Warton facility. A separate March training and support agreement provides for 10 Turkish pilots and nearly 100 ground crew technicians to train in the UK. Ankara has also been negotiating with Qatar and Oman to acquire secondhand Eurofighters that could enter service sooner.
sections.whyItMatters: The start of flight training moves Turkey's Eurofighter acquisition from contract to capability, giving Ankara a Western fighter option alongside its indigenous KAAN programme and reducing reliance on any single supplier.

sections.heading: Defense Industry: MKE Enters Egyptian Market With Cairo Subsidiary
sections.body:
Turkish state-run defense manufacturer Machinery and Chemical Industry (MKE) has established a wholly owned subsidiary in Cairo under Egyptian law, Daily Sabah reports. The move deepens the defense-industrial relationship between Ankara and Cairo, which has expanded significantly since the two countries normalized ties.

MKE, a major producer of ammunition, explosives and small arms, joins a growing list of Turkish defense firms seeking footholds in the Egyptian market. The subsidiary gives MKE a local presence to pursue contracts and partnerships as Egypt modernizes its defense industrial base.
sections.whyItMatters: A Turkish state arms maker establishing a permanent presence in Egypt signals that the Ankara-Cairo defense relationship is moving beyond one-off sales toward deeper industrial integration — a notable shift for two countries that were adversaries a decade ago.

sections.heading: Foreign Relations: Cyprus Talks Stall as TRNC Leader Urges End to Trust-Eroding Steps
sections.body:
Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC) President Tufan Erhürman said he and Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides failed to reach an agreement on new confidence-building measures after their latest talks, Daily Sabah reports. Erhürman urged an end to steps that erode trust between the two sides.

The stalled talks come as the Cyprus issue remains a persistent irritant in Turkey's relations with Greece and the EU. Separately, Daily Sabah reports Greece's expanding defense alliances and armament programs are fueling concerns they may come at odds with Türkiye, with which it still has a lingering Aegean dispute.
sections.whyItMatters: With no breakthrough on confidence-building measures, the Cyprus track remains frozen, while Greece's naval buildup keeps the Aegean dimension of the rivalry in play — two fronts where Ankara sees little near-term movement.

sections.heading: Domestic: CHP Marks 103 Years With Dimming Prospects; Üsküdar Takeover Draws EU Criticism
sections.body:
The Republican People's Party (CHP) marked its 103rd anniversary Wednesday with top officials visiting Anıtkabir, Daily Sabah reports, in a year of internal turmoil. The party's prospects look dimmer after a court-appointed leadership restructuring and the arrest of İstanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, which reshaped the opposition landscape.

Separately, European Parliament rapporteur on Turkey Nacho Sánchez Amor called the AKP's return to power in İstanbul's Üsküdar Municipality a 'blatant power grab', Turkish Minute reports. The AKP's Dündar Ziya Gültekin defeated CHP's Sibel Tan Çetinkaya 23-19 in the fourth round of voting, after four opposition council members defected and two were arrested. The vote followed the July 31 arrest of CHP Mayor Sinem Dedetaş. Sánchez Amor said the 'whole system was perverted in order to win what was lost at the ballot box.'
sections.whyItMatters: The CHP's anniversary lands amid a leadership crisis and a high-profile municipal loss in Üsküdar that has drawn sharp EU criticism — a reminder that the opposition's legal and political setbacks are compounding as it tries to rebuild ahead of the next national vote.

bottomLine: Today's developments put the US-Turkey relationship at the center: Washington sanctioned three Turkish firms over Iran-linked aviation and logistics activity under 'Operation Economic Outcast,' even as Erdoğan hosted US envoy Tom Barrack for talks on Syria and Iraq. The dual-track approach — financial pressure alongside diplomatic engagement — is now the defining pattern of the bilateral relationship. Meanwhile, the PKK disarmament process moved toward a concrete staged plan in Erbil, with Qandil deliberately deferred and the question of who collects the weapons still unresolved. On defense, Turkish pilots began Eurofighter flight training in the UK and MKE opened a Cairo subsidiary, deepening both Western and Egyptian defense ties. The CHP's 103rd anniversary was overshadowed by the Üsküdar municipal loss and EU criticism, while Cyprus talks stalled and Greece's naval buildup kept the Aegean rivalry in view.
sources: Turkish Minute, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency, Al Aalem Al Jadid, Middle East Eye, US Treasury OFAC
